name: Georgian National Museum
watch: BP, a name under active campaign, is a current and long-running funder. On 5 Oct 2026 the museum.ge homepage footer carries a BP logo linking to bpgeorgia.ge, and the site has a dedicated 'BP' corporate-partner page. The museum's 2010 volume 'Rescue Archaeology in Georgia: Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan / South Caucasian Pipelines' thanks BP and its partners and has BP Georgia staff on its editorial board. Separately, in May 2022 about 40 staff were dismissed under minister Thea Tsulukiani; they alleged retaliation for criticising the government and forming a union (ArtReview).

name: Musée Théodore Monod d'Art Africain (IFAN)
watch: The museum's own partners page (musee-monod.sn/nos-partenaires, read Oct 2026) lists Fondation TOTAL Sénégal among current partners. TotalEnergies is an excluded funder under active campaign. Other partners: Fondation SOCOCIM (cement), Gerda Henkel, Volkswagen Foundation, the French Embassy, Goethe-Institut and Grand Palais RMN.

name: Villa des Arts de Casablanca
watch: The founding and current funder is Al Mada, through its foundation. Al Mada owns 100% of Nareva, which holds 50.7% of the 1,386 MW Safi coal-fired power station. That makes a fossil-fuel (coal) owner the current and founding funder. No protest at the villa was found.
why_flagged: The founding and current funder is Al Mada, through its foundation. Al Mada owns 100% of Nareva, which holds 50.7% of the 1,386 MW Safi coal-fired power station. Nareva raised its stake by buying ENGIE shares in January 2025, and GEM reports Al Mada was set to take full control in October 2025. That makes a fossil-fuel (coal) owner the current and founding funder. No protest at the villa was found.
records_note: The villa's site sits behind a bot check and its Fondation Al Mada parent site did not load, so nothing could be checked.

name: Greenland National Museum and Archives (Nunatta Katersugaasivia Allagaateqarfialu)
watch: Excluded funder is current. The 2024 annual report records a DKK 4.5M grant from Augustinus Fonden (a Scandinavian Tobacco Group holder) for the 3-year Angerlartunnguit research project on the Uunartoq Thule Inuit. It also records a DKK 300,000 Augustinus grant for the PoTraCh airport documentation and Augustinus co-funding of the Qimmit project (2023-26).

name: School of Visual Arts
watch: Ross chaired SVA's MFA Art Practice department from 2009. In October 2009 Epstein proposed a "statutory" exhibition of "girls and boys ages 14 - 25", and Ross replied, "You are incredible."
why_flagged: Private art school in Manhattan. The Rhodes family owned it until 1 September 2025; the nonprofit SVA Alumni Society owns it now. No sponsor list found.
records_note: sva.edu posts no annual report, financial statements or donor list but names its 10-person board of trustees; no filings under the school's own name.
other_findings: Epstein link · David A. Ross · documented: Ross, a former director of the Whitney, SFMOMA and ICA Boston, stayed close friends with Epstein after his 2008 conviction, kept in contact until at least 2016 and says he contacted Epstein again in 2019. SVA accepted his resignation, effective 3 February 2026, after a student petition.

name: SFMOMA
watch: In 2001, while David A. Ross was director, SFMOMA acquired a 20% interest in John F. Simon Jr.'s ComplexCity (2000), recorded as a "fractional and promised gift of Jeffrey Epstein". In 2009 director Neal Benezra wrote to thank Epstein for his "continued support".
why_flagged: Foundation and government list (June 2025): Ford, Warhol, Luce, Haas, Hearst, Koret and Osher foundations, Grants for the Arts, NEA and IMLS. No corporate sponsor list published.
records_note: Annual reports on its site run 2011 to 2018; Form 990s and audits are on ProPublica, foundation funders are named (June 2025) and trustees listed.
other_findings: Epstein link · Jeffrey Epstein · documented: SFMOMA says the 2009 letter was standard donor language and it has no record of support from Epstein after 2001. The work was never exhibited; the museum deaccessioned it in October 2019 and returned its share to the artist. | Epstein link · Neri Oxman · documented: Oxman's Vespers II was shown in her 2022 SFMOMA exhibition "Nature x Humanity". Emails in the 2026 DOJ release show she thanked Epstein in 2017 for supporting her Vespers "death masks", and in December 2017 he agreed by email to give $25,000 toward a follow-on project. Epstein gave $125,000 to Oxman's MIT design lab in 2017, and she apologised in 2019. SFMOMA's curator did not respond.

name: New York Academy of Art
watch: Epstein sat on the Academy's board from 1987 to 1994 and met student Maria Farmer there in 1995; Farmer reported him to the FBI in 1996, the first report against him. After his 2008 conviction he bought a $25,000 table at the Academy's Tribeca Ball in 2012 and in 2014, gave $30,000 for scholarship support in 2014, and attended Academy events.
why_flagged: Van Cleef & Arpels sponsors its Tribeca Ball for scholarships. Epstein, a board member 1987 to 1994, paid $65,900 for events in 2012 and 2014, the Academy says.
records_note: Its site names 29 trustees but posts no annual report, financial statements or donor list; Form 990s and a 2025 audit are on ProPublica.
other_findings: Epstein link · Jeffrey Epstein · documented: In March 2026 the Academy admitted "serious failures", said it would give $65,900 linked to the 2012 and 2014 events to GEMS, and set up an ethics committee. It had given GEMS $30,000 in 2020. | Epstein link · Eileen Guggenheim · documented: Eileen Guggenheim was the Academy's dean in 1995 and later its board chair. Emails show that after Epstein's 2008 conviction she encouraged his support of the school, and in 2014 he gave $30,000 for scholarships at her invitation. Maria Farmer alleges that Guggenheim introduced her to Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell at her 1995 thesis show, pressed her to sell Epstein a painting at a steep discount and ignored her complaints; Guggenheim denies "the substance and odious implications" of the allegations. The Academy commissioned a report that disputed Farmer's claims. In March 2026 it said it should not have taken Epstein's money or let him attend events, and Guggenheim brought her retirement forward by a month, to April 2026.

name: Interlochen Center for the Arts
watch: Epstein attended Interlochen's summer camp in 1967 and gave money to it from 1990 to 2003, including a $200,000 gift, acknowledged in February 1994, for a lodge on Green Lake named after him. A witness at Ghislaine Maxwell's 2021 trial and a second woman say Epstein and Maxwell met them at the camp at 13 and 14, from 1994, and DOJ files show the pair met a student alone at the lodge.
why_flagged: Private nonprofit arts academy and camp. Gifts were $24.1M in fiscal 2025. Its 2025 report names trustee David Wu, the Foster Family Foundation, DeRoy Testamentary Foundation and Walker Foundation.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2020 to 2026 and audited statements for 2020 to 2024, with named funds in the 2025 report and 31 trustees.
other_findings: Epstein link · Jeffrey Epstein · documented: Interlochen renamed the building Green Lake Lodge in 2009 and says reviews in 2009 and 2019 found no evidence of crimes on campus. In May 2026 it announced it would tear the lodge down. In July 2026 a Sanghavi Law Office report recorded two women's accounts that Epstein engaged in sexual conduct with them, one of them at the lodge.
